rv.q: Actually, it’s more like three – making it a 360, all-round, head-spinning winner.

Mischief’s artistic director, Lewis co-wrote the script with Wright, and there are many of their fellow founders – who all studied together at LAMDA – and trusted regulars from previous shows in the cast. Dave Hearn’s elastic Lance, Chris Leask’s strangulated Sergei and Greg Tannahill’s fey hotel ma...
It is impossible not to be swept along by the giddily escalating mirth of Matt DiCarlo’s amiable production.
I’d say it takes near genius to fashion something this incorrigibly goofy.
For bungling wit matched with peerless physical comedy, you'd be hard pressed to find better in the West End.
I was crying helpless tears of laughter within the first five minutes, and at several other moments throughout.
But while the physical comedy is impeccably executed, the bare-bones story it’s running on will leave some craving a little more substance.
It can feel as if five shows’ worth of slapstick and farce has been crammed into one, which is a mixed blessing.
This finely tuned machine of comic timing and theatrical chaos is possibly Mischief’s best work yet, offering audiences exactly what they have come to expect – and love – from this troupe.
If you like Mischief's previous work, you will love this.
Farce this slick, this tongue-in-cheek, this quirkily British, will always draw laughter from a hugely appreciative audience.
Mischief is a creative, comedic powerhouse, and the clever storyline and talented cast make About Spies not only a spectacular spy spoof but also an outstanding show altogether.

About Spies is wonderful stuff, and highly amusing: this is a production company that has honed their craft, and their experience shines through in what is probably their most sophisticated show yet, at least in its technical aspects.
What could easily have come off the rails is majestically held together by Matt DiCarlo’s razor-sharp direction.
Their latest show, an espionage spoof, improvised and scripted, strong on wordplay, is as silly and as funny and as absurd as their past productions.
This is an evening of daft, uncomplicated fun.
This is clearly going to be an enormous popular hit.
Without a doubt, the funniest show I have seen in years and the funniest show I’d expect anyone to see this year.
It genuinely is one of the most amusing shows to infiltrate the West End in years.
Mischief Comedy’s latest theatrical assault on the funny bone is riotously entertaining, breathtakingly well executed and, quite simply, one of the funniest shows I have seen in a very long time.
About Spies is more than just a comedy; it's a masterclass in theatrical entertainment.
Just book a ticket. It's smart, silly, fast-paced fun that'll leave your face aching from laughing. Pure spy spoof perfection.
A delightfully daft show filled to the brim with laughs, I dare say that About Spies is among Mischief Theatre's best works.
Mischief at their best, as finely worked as clockwork and exuberant as toddlers.
About Spies is an absolutely stellar show from its production to its performance.
This show will keep you chuckling.
If what you want is to switch off, relax, and spend a thoroughly enjoyable evening at the theatre, this is an excellent choice.
The scriptwriting, the set design, the acting, everything comes together to produce an excellent comedy with great twists at the end.
About Spies delivers with all the Mischief Theatre charm with clever writing, witty and playful humour and fantastic acting.

Mischief take on a fresh genre to parody in About Spies that does a good job of combining the company’s classic style of comedy with a heartfelt and intriguing plot, making for an entertaining couple of hours in the theatre.
It's an impressive irony that such farcical events have been so meticulously planned.
Mischief fans and newbies alike will find plenty to enjoy here and will undoubtably refer to this as one of the company's greatest shows to date.
If you are looking for pure, unadulterated escapism, About Spies certainly delivers on laughs.
A riot from start to finish, minutely planned, plotted and executed, with blisteringly good performances and every opportunity taken to make you laugh.
With its sharpened script, superb cast and relentless silliness, About Spies proves this is a spy mission well worth revisiting.

Equal parts side-splittingly funny and gasp-worthy, the play (that definitely went right) truly goes above and beyond expectations, a creative stroke of genius in what can be accomplished in a comedy play.
This gloriously British romp will have you laughing so hard you’ll blow your cover.
The second act is where the pace begins to drift.

cn.t: Mischief Theatre delivers another riotously funny hit with rapid-fire wordplay, precision slapstick, and chaotic Cold War espionage. Critics praise the expertly crafted farce, though some find the puns groan-worthy and formula familiar.
